newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up led by local firms.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up led by local firms.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index rebounded on Friday led by strong performing Shenzhen-based companies, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index rose 0.85 points or 0.49 percent to 176.64 on turnover of HK$144.9 million against Thursday's HK$156.6 million.
Analysts said investors favoured companies based in Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, because of strong economic prospects for the area ahead of the British colony's handover on July 1.
"As the Hong Kong handover draws near, people are focusing on companies that may gain from it," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Gintian Co was the best performer, rising HK$0.17 or 4.15 percent to HK$4.27.
China Vanke Co Ltd, also a Shenzhen-based conglomerate, was the second biggest gainer, adding HK$0.34 or 3.84 percent to HK$9.20.
"I would expect these Shenzhen-based stocks to play an important role towards the handover and after," an analyst at a western investment bank said.
The index is likely to pick up next week and move steadily higher, analysts said.
"Investor caution after recent sharp gains seems to have faded," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
Trading volume picked up in the afternoon, suggesting the index will move higher next week, analysts said.
The A share index gained 2.34 points or 0.49 percent to close at 483.85 on turnover of 17.8 billion yuan against 14.0 billion yuan on Thursday.
